topic_text: The value of goods and services produced in the UK.
text:
UK business investment increased by 3.9% in Quarter 1 (Jan to Mar) 2025, revised down from a 5.9% increase in the provisional estimate.

The largest contributors to the increase in business investment were increases in transport equipment and ICT equipment and other machinery and equipment, partially offset by decreases in intellectual property products (IPP).

UK business investment is 6.1% above the level seen in the same quarter a year ago.

UK whole economy investment (technically known as gross fixed capital formation (GFCF)), which includes business and public sector investment, increased by 2.0% in Quarter 1 2025, revised down from a 2.9% increase in the provisional estimate.

topic_text: How much the production and services industries contribute to economic output.
text:
Monthly production output was estimated to have decreased 0.9% in May 2025; this follows falls in April 2025 (down 0.6%) and March 2025 (down 0.2%).

The fall in monthly output in May 2025 resulted from decreases in "manufacturing" (down 1.0%) and "mining and quarrying" (down 3.2%); these were partially offset by an increase in "water supply and sewerage" (up 0.8%) and "electricity and gas" (up 0.3%).

9 of the 13 manufacturing subsectors saw a fall in May 2025, with the largest negative contribution coming from "basic pharmaceutical products" (down 4.2%); with other negative contributions from "transport equipment" (down 1.3%) and "basic metals and metal products" (down 1.8%).

Production output was estimated to have increased (up 0.2%) during the three months to May 2025, compared with the three months to February 2025; this is mainly because of a weak December and January 2025 level, followed by a strong February 2025.

The largest positive contributor to the three-monthly rise in May 2025 came from "water supply and sewerage" (up 3.7%), supported by "manufacturing" (up 0.4%); this was partially offset by decreases in "electricity and gas" (down 2.8%) and "mining and quarrying" (down 1.6%).

Monthly services output was estimated to have grown by 0.1% in May 2025; this follows a fall of 0.3% in April 2025 and a rise of 0.4% in March 2025.

There were monthly increases in 10 of the 14 sectors in May 2025; the largest positive contribution came from "information and communication" (up 2.0%).

The monthly increase in output was partially offset by monthly decreases in 4 of the 14 sectors in May 2025; the largest negative contribution came from "wholesale and retail activities" (down 1.5%).

The two industries that mainly contributed to the monthly rise in May 2025 were "legal services" (up 6.1%) and "computer programming, consultancy and related activities" (up 3.0%); the main offsetting negative contribution at an industry level was in "retail trade" (down 2.7%).

text:

More broadly sales volumes rose by 0.2% in Quarter 2 (Apr to June) 2025 when compared with Quarter 1 (Jan to Mar) 2025.

topic_text: Changes in prices of goods and services bought by consumers, as well as those bought and sold by producers in the UK.
text:
The Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs (CPIH) 12-month inflation rate was 4.1% in June 2025, up from 4.0% in May 2025.

Consumer price inflation can be influenced by the strength of domestic supply and demand, and changes in the UK prices of imports. The inflation rate also depends on price levels in the preceding year.

Producer output (factory gate) prices rose by 0.3% in the year to January 2025, up from a revised fall of 0.1% in the year to December 2024.

Changes in the output Producer Price Index inflation rate can be influenced by changes in labour and energy costs.

Producer input prices fell by 0.1% in the year to January 2025, up from a revised fall of 1.3% in the year to December 2024.

Input prices are influenced by raw material prices and exchange rate movements so are more changeable over time than output prices.

topic_text: UK exports and imports of goods and services and measures of foreign direct investment.
text:
The value of goods imports increased by £0.6 billion (1.2%) in May 2025, with a rise in imports from both EU and non-EU countries.

The value of goods exports increased by £0.6 billion (2.2%) in May 2025, with an increase in exports to both EU and non-EU countries.

Exports of goods to the United States, including precious metals, rose by £0.3 billion in May 2025 following a substantial decrease the previous month, and remained relatively low.

The total goods and services trade deficit widened by £6.7 billion to £13.2 billion in the three months to May 2025, because of a large rise in goods imports and a fall in goods exports.

The trade in goods deficit widened by £6.1 billion to £61.0 billion in the three months to May 2025, while the trade in services surplus is estimated to have narrowed by £0.6 billion to £47.8 billion.

text: UK direct investment liabilities were £2,455.3 billion in October to December 2024, up slightly from £2,394.1 billion in the previous quarter. FDI liabilities have been following a broadly downward trend in the last two years.

UK direct investment assets were £2,206.1 billion in October to December 2024, up slightly from £2,166.7 billion in the previous quarter. The value of FDI assets has been following a broadly downward trend since early 2023.
